title: Guava & Cheese Strudel (Pastelitos De Guayaba Y Queso)
description: Flakey, gooey, and buttery homemade guava and cheese strudels are easier to make than you would imagine. Follow this recipe to learn how to make your own guava jam, shortcut puff pastry, and cheese filling!

steps.text: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, add the pureed guava and sugar. Use a wooden spoon or spatula to incorporate the sugar completely. Bring the mixture to a boil.

steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and simmer the mixture for about 15 minutes or until the guava mixture has reduced by about half. steps.text: Roll out each of the dough pieces into a long rectangle of about 14 by 10 inches with a thickness of ¼ inch. Divide each of the rectangles into 6 pieces (if you want large strudels) or 12 pieces (if you want medium sized strudels). Place half of these rectangles in a parchment paper lined sheet pan with at least one inch space between them.

steps.text: In a small bowl, beat one egg. Brush the egg wash on the edges of half of the rectangles (the bottom halves of your pastries), about ¼” thick around the perimeter.

steps.text: Spread the cheese filling in the center of the egg-washed rectangles.

steps.text: Add guava jam on top, both spread evenly close to but not touching the egg wash.

steps.text: For the untouched rectangles, these are the pastry tops. Cut 2-3 slits in the center for venting and added design. Then carefully take one of these rectangles and place it on top of a filled guava and cheese piece. Carefully press the edges and seal them using a fork.

steps.text: Brush more egg wash on top. Optional: sprinkle some turbinado sugar on top for extra texture. Repeat with the rest of the strudels.

steps.text: Place the sheet pan and strudels in the middle rack of the oven and bake for 20-30 minutes. I would recommend checking the pastries at 15 minutes to check on them. Remove from the oven when they are puffy and golden brown at the edges and top.

review.reviewBody: Soooo yummy and very easy to make, especially if you use frozen puff pastry and guava jam (I used Bonne Maman's). I'm sure it'd be even better if you make both yourself. It ended up tasting exactly like Porto's Refugiado's (arguably better) and they were super delicious!!
